item.title: Hoax bomb threats force emergency landings, evacuations across Europe
item.description:
Bomb hoaxers turned European skies into chaos on Thursday. At least 14 passenger jets were hit with phony threats, and fighter jets were scrambled to shadow the planes to the ground. It was the third wave of the madness this week. An Aer Lingus jet bound from Dublin to Rome was abruptly yanked off course and escorted by French military aircraft to the Évreux air base west of Paris. The office of French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said it was keeping close watch. Over Italy, air force jets locked onto Finnair Flight 1761 from Helsinki and escorted it into Rome’s Fiumicino Airport, where a bomb squad tore through the plane. They found nothing . The chaos spread fast. Three Ryanair flights bound for Sofia, Bulgaria, were targeted, and one from London was diverted to Plovdiv. Four planes headed to Prague, flown by Ryanair, easyJet, and Sky Express, were threatened in anonymous emails.…

item.title: What comes next for Democrats after midterm election victory?
item.description:
A lot of funny things happened last night during the midterms, in what can only be read as a rejection of the Trump admin specifically, but perhaps the funniest detail is that the composers of both the Dragon Ball Z dub and the game Halo won and lost their races respectively. America has spoken: Yes to the dub of Dragon Ball Z , no to Halo . The incumbent in Nevada’s 3rd district, Democrat Susie Lee, beat composer and repeat loser Marty O’Donnell. (O’Donnell previously came in fourth in the 2024 Republican primary, losing to Drew Johnson, who went on to lose to Susie Lee.) O’Donnell co-composed soundtrack for the Halo series as well as the first Destiny game along with Michael Salvatori–despite how you might feel about whatever soundtracks he put out in the past, he has a fairly awful record politically. He has a history of wildly sexist comments and has hosted many questionable guests…

item.title: US elections 2026 live: Democrats hold nearly 100 more House seats than Republicans as blue wave continues to grow
item.description:
In summary Democrats notched big wins across the country, even in deep red districts that Republicans in Texas, Florida and North Carolina had gerrymandered to benefit their own party. That begs the question — did California really need to toss aside its independent redistricting commission? California Democrats went all in on redistricting last year in a rebuke of President Donald Trump’s call for Republicans to gerrymander red states and preserve their U.S. House majority. Ultimately, though, it appears such a gamble wasn’t even necessary. The “blue tsunami” that engulfed the country was enough to sweep away Republicans in ruby-red districts that Trump won by double digits two years ago as Democrats improved on their 2024 margin by a stunning 15 percentage points. At least five of California’s nine-member Republican delegation were among the political casualties. It’s not clear yet…

item.title: Washington state passes ballot measure banning trans girls from school sports
item.description:
Nebraska and Arizona have passed ballot measures to ban transgender student-athletes from playing on girls’ sports teams, marking a significant referendum on trans rights. As of Wednesday morning, similar ballot measures in Colorado and Washington are still undecided, although early projections suggest that the measures will pass in both states. Nebraska was the only state to add language explicitly directed toward trans students to its state code. The measure , introduced in January, qualified for the general election in August, after organizers collected more than 200,000 signatures from across the state. Nebraska law already prohibits trans student-athletes from participating in sports in line with their gender identity from kindergarten through college. item.title: South Africa’s ANC on track for new lows in local polls
item.description:
Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure. The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party. However, polls showed it getting less than a third of the vote, down from 45.6% at the last municipal elections in 2021 and 40.2% in 2024’s national elections . Continue reading...

item.title: Russian and Ukrainian officials thank Melania Trump for brokering ceasefire - video
item.description:
Photo Illustration by Thomas Levinson/The Daily Beast/Reuters Melania Trump praised the Russians; she praised the Ukrainians; she touted her senior adviser; but she didn’t mention her husband, Donald Trump, at her event on Thursday. The first lady held the gathering at the White House to celebrate the temporary ceasefire deal in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, which concluded on November 1. It came as the president has come up short on his own promise to bring about an end to the war in Ukraine, which has been raging since Russia invaded in 2022. He previously claimed he could end the war on day one of his second term. Read more at The Daily Beast.

item.title: Anti-Trans Panic Couldn’t Save Republicans in Deep-Red Texas
item.description:
On an election night handing Republicans a beating in critical House and Senate races across the country, the GOP fell short even in once deep-red Texas after a campaign run on a go-to outrage tactic: fearmongering over the rights of transgender people. Democrats escaped the political wilderness in the Longhorn State on Tuesday night, when Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton — despite the far-right attorney general’s relentless attacks on the trans community and his party’s claims that Democrats would enforce so-called “transgenderism” as a kind of ideology. item.title: America Finally Has the Votes to End the Electoral College
item.description:
Tuesday’s wave election swept Democrats into power in Congress. But the most seismic result for American politics and democracy may come out of the battleground states where Democrats just won trifecta control by taking both state houses and the governor’s mansion: Come January, Democratic legislators will have the votes to elect the next president by the popular vote. State lawmakers could circumvent the Electoral College by enacting what’s known as the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact . Under the current system, each state gets a set number of electors, and the candidate who wins enough states to accumulate at least 270 electoral votes becomes president. This system allows the winner of the popular vote to lose, as Al Gore did in 2000 and Hillary Clinton again in 2016.
